 Senate Act Would Boost Loan Forgiveness to $17,500 for EL Teachers
 November 9, 2026 
 Tags: 
 teachers 
 language 
 news 
 EL 
 loan forgiveness 
 0 shares 
 US Senators Alex Padilla (D-California), Andy Kim (D-New Jersey), Brian Schatz (D-Hawaii), and Adam Schiff (D-California) have introduced the Supporting Providers of English Language Learning (SPELL) Act to help address the national multilingual teacher shortage by increasing loan forgiveness from $5,000 to $17,500 for teachers of English Learners (ELs). Representatives Adriano Espaillat (D-New York) and Adelita Grijalva (D-Arizona) introduced companion legislation in the House of Representatives.
 Currently, if a highly qualified teacher has been employed for five consecutive years in a low-income school, they are eligible for up to $5,000 of student loan forgiveness. Certain teachers who go into high-demand subjects are eligible for an increased benefit of $17,500 of student loan forgiveness. Recognizing the growing EL teacher shortage, theSPELL Act adds EL teachers to this high-demand category, making them eligible for additional debt relief.
 The Department of Education has reported that 32 states have a shortage of teachers for EL students, making them unable to meet students’ needs and resulting in a discouraging academic achievement gap for this growing population. The cost of teacher preparation programs can be an obstacle for many to enter the profession, but data shows an association between teachers’ preparation level and their teaching effectiveness and retention. Research demonstrates that loan forgiveness programs are successful at encouraging teachers to take positions in fields and at locations where they are most needed, and forgiveness programs also help to support retention.
 Specifically, the bill would provide up to $17,500 in loan forgiveness for teachers of ELs, bilingual students, and/or dual language immersion students. This matches the same level of enhanced forgiveness available to math, science, and special education teachers.
 The SPELL Act is endorsed by organizations including TESOL, AFT, UnidosUS, and the California Community Colleges.
 “At a time when the Trump administration seems intent on attacking English Language Learners, public school educators continue to fulfill their mission to serve each and every child who comes through their classroom door,” commented AFT president Randi Weingarten. “ELL teachers have dedicated their lives to helping kids, but student debt and the cost of living are dragging them down. The Supporting Providers of English Language Learning Act would allow ELL teachers to qualify for the highest level of teacher loan forgiveness so they can pursue their careers free from the specter of permanent student debt.”   In June, Padilla led Senate colleagues in condemning the Trump administration’s attacks on English Learners and the dissolution of the Department of Education’s Office of English Language Acquisition (OELA).
